props.text: One chainring at the front, seven sprockets at the back and a derailleur that moves the chain between them. Small sprockets make each pedal stroke go further; big ones make hills easier.

rows: Hold everything together, steer and set the riding position
The single front gear, here 40 teeth
Carries the power to the rear wheel
Seven sizes, so seven gear ratios
Moves the chain from sprocket to sprocket
Pull or release the cable to pick a gear
Stop, roll and grip the road

props.text: The shifter pulls a cable; the derailleur guides the chain onto the sprocket you choose.
Each turn of the pedals turns the rear wheel 1.9 times. Balanced effort for flat roads and everyday riding.
Assumes a 40-tooth chainring, a 12-28 freewheel and a 700c wheel (2.1 m around). Real bikes vary.
The ratchet sits inside the sprocket cluster, which screws onto the hub. Common on budget and youth bikes.
The sprockets slide onto a freehub that holds the ratchet. Better axle support and easy gear swaps.
Seven speeds keep the drivetrain simple, light and cheap to maintain: one shifter, one derailleur and no front gear changes to think about.
